stemBlocks.value: Line segments AC and BD intersect at O, with AO = OC and BO = OD. a) Prove that triangle AOB is congruent to triangle COD, stating the congruence case used. b) Hence prove that AB = CD. c) Use a pair of equal alternate angles to show that AB is parallel to CD.
Think first: The crossing point O gives you a pair of vertically opposite angles, which is exactly the angle wedged between the two given equal sides.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p166-q04 from workbook page 166.

solutionSteps.instruction: List the equal parts of triangles AOB and COD.

contentBlocks.value: AO = OC (given); ∠AOB = ∠COD (vertically opposite angles); BO = OD (given)
Two sides and the angle between them are equal

solutionSteps.instruction: Read off the third pair of sides.

contentBlocks.value: AB and CD are corresponding sides of the congruent triangles

solutionSteps.instruction: Read off a pair of corresponding angles at A and C.
Interpret those angles for the line AC.

contentBlocks.value: AC is a transversal cutting AB and CD, and ∠BAO and ∠DCO are alternate angles; equal alternate angles mean the lines are parallel
Result: AB is parallel to CD

strategyBlocks.value: Pair the two given equal sides with the vertically opposite angle between them to get SAS, then read off equal corresponding sides and angles.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a) Triangle AOB ≅ triangle COD by SAS (AO = OC, ∠AOB = ∠COD vertically opposite, BO = OD)  (b) AB = CD as corresponding sides of congruent triangles  (c) ∠BAO = ∠DCO are equal alternate angles for AB and CD with transversal AC, so AB is parallel to CD

whyThisWorks.value: SAS works because fixing two sides and the angle wedged between them leaves no freedom in the third side. The vertically opposite angle is the key: it is equal automatically wherever two straight lines cross, so the diagram supplies the middle ingredient without it being stated. Part c then runs the alternate-angle rule backwards — equal alternate angles are not just a consequence of parallel lines, they are a test for them.

commonErrors.misconception: Using ∠OAB and ∠OCD as the included angle — the included angle must be at O, between the two given sides.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Using ∠OAB and ∠OCD as the included angle — the included angle must be at O, between the two given sides.

examTip.value: Whenever two lines cross in a proof diagram, immediately mark the vertically opposite angles as equal — that free fact completes most SAS proofs.
